[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5f/1951_CECA_ECSC.jpg/250px-1951_CECA_ECSC.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1951_CECA_ECSC.jpg)

[Treaty of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Paris_(1951) "Treaty of Paris (1951)") (1951), establishing the [ECSC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Coal_and_Steel_Community "European Coal and Steel Community")

Immediately following the [February 1948 coup d'état](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Czechoslovak_coup_d'%C3%A9tat "1948 Czechoslovak coup d'état") by the [Communist Party of Czechoslovakia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_Czechoslovakia "Communist Party of Czechoslovakia"), the [London Six-Power Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Six-Power_Conference "London Six-Power Conference") was held, resulting in the [Soviet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") boycott of the Allied Control Council and its incapacitation, an event marking the beginning of the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War"). The year 1948 marked the beginning of the institutionalised modern [European integration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_integration "European integration"). In March 1948 the [Treaty of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Brussels "Treaty of Brussels") was signed, establishing the [Western Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Union_(alliance) "Western Union (alliance)") (WU), followed by the [International Authority for the Ruhr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Authority_for_the_Ruhr "International Authority for the Ruhr"). Furthermore, the [Organisation for European Economic Co-operation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisation_for_European_Economic_Co-operation "Organisation for European Economic Co-operation") (OEEC), the predecessor of the OECD, was also founded in 1948 to manage the [Marshall Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_Plan "Marshall Plan"), which led to the Soviets creating [Comecon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comecon "Comecon") in response. The ensuing [Hague Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hague_Congress_(1948) "Hague Congress (1948)") of May 1948 was a pivotal moment in European integration, as it led to the creation of the [European Movement International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Movement_International "European Movement International"), the [College of Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_of_Europe "College of Europe"),[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-34) and most importantly to the foundation of the [Council of Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_Europe "Council of Europe") on 5 May 1949 (which is now [Europe Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe_Day "Europe Day")). The Council of Europe has since been a broad forum to further cooperation and shared issues, achieving, for example, the [European Convention on Human Rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Convention_on_Human_Rights "European Convention on Human Rights") in 1950.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-35)

Essential for the actual birth of the institutions of the EU was the [Schuman Declaration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schuman_Declaration "Schuman Declaration") on 9 May 1950 (the day after the fifth [Victory in Europe Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victory_in_Europe_Day "Victory in Europe Day")) and the decision by six nations (France, Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg, West Germany, and Italy) to follow Schuman and draft the [Treaty of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Paris_(1951) "Treaty of Paris (1951)"). This treaty was created in 1952 the [European Coal and Steel Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Coal_and_Steel_Community "European Coal and Steel Community") (ECSC), which was built on the [International Authority for the Ruhr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Authority_for_the_Ruhr "International Authority for the Ruhr"), installed by the Western Allies in 1949 to regulate the coal and steel industries of the Ruhr area in West Germany.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-36) Backed by the [Marshall Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_Plan "Marshall Plan") with large funds coming from the United States since 1948, the ECSC became a milestone organisation, enabling European economic development and integration and being the origin of the main institutions of the EU such as the [European Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Commission "European Commission") and [Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Parliament "European Parliament").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-37)

The [founding fathers of the European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Founding_fathers_of_the_European_Union "Founding fathers of the European Union") understood that coal and steel were the two industries essential for waging war, and believed that by tying their national industries together, a future war between their nations became much less likely.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-Europa_History_45-59-38) In parallel with Schuman, the [Pleven Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleven_Plan "Pleven Plan") of 1951 tried but failed to tie the institutions of the developing European community under the [European Political Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Political_Community_(1952) "European Political Community (1952)"), which was to include the also proposed [European Defence Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_establishing_the_European_Defence_Community "Treaty establishing the European Defence Community"), an alternative to [West Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Germany "West Germany") joining [NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO "NATO") which was established in 1949 under the [Truman Doctrine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Truman_Doctrine "Truman Doctrine"). In 1954 the [Modified Brussels Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modified_Brussels_Treaty "Modified Brussels Treaty") transformed the Western Union into the [Western European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_European_Union "Western European Union") (WEU). West Germany eventually joined both the WEU and NATO in 1955, prompting the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") to form the [Warsaw Pact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warsaw_Pact "Warsaw Pact") in 1955 as an institutional framework for its military domination in the countries of [Central and Eastern Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_and_Eastern_Europe "Central and Eastern Europe"). Assessing the progress of European integration the [Messina Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Messina_Conference "Messina Conference") was held in 1955, ordering the [Spaak Report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spaak_Report "Spaak Report"), which in 1956 recommended the next significant steps of European integration.

### Treaty of Rome (1958‍–‍1972)

Main article: [History of the European Communities (1958–1972)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_European_Communities_(1958%E2%80%931972) "History of the European Communities (1958–1972)")

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/59/Bundesarchiv_Bild_183-45653-0001%2C_Rom%2C_Vertr%C3%A4ge_%C3%BCber_Zollpakt_und_Eurotom_unterzeichnet.jpg/250px-Bundesarchiv_Bild_183-45653-0001%2C_Rom%2C_Vertr%C3%A4ge_%C3%BCber_Zollpakt_und_Eurotom_unterzeichnet.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bundesarchiv_Bild_183-45653-0001,_Rom,_Vertr%C3%A4ge_%C3%BCber_Zollpakt_und_Eurotom_unterzeichnet.jpg)

Signing ceremony of the [Treaty of Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Rome "Treaty of Rome") (1957), establishing the [EEC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Economic_Community "European Economic Community")

In 1957, [Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium "Belgium"), [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France"), [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy"), [Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxembourg "Luxembourg"), [the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands"), and [West Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Germany "West Germany") signed the [Treaty of Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Rome "Treaty of Rome"), which created the [European Economic Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Economic_Community "European Economic Community") (EEC) and established a [customs union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union_Customs_Union "European Union Customs Union").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-39) They also signed another pact creating the [European Atomic Energy Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Atomic_Energy_Community "European Atomic Energy Community") (Euratom) for cooperation in developing nuclear power. Both treaties came into force in 1958.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-Europa_History_45-59-38) Although the EEC and Euratom were created separately from the ECSC, they shared the same courts and the Common Assembly. The EEC was headed by [Walter Hallstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Hallstein "Walter Hallstein") ([Hallstein Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hallstein_Commission "Hallstein Commission")) and Euratom was headed by [Louis Armand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Armand "Louis Armand") ([Armand Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armand_Commission "Armand Commission")) and then [Étienne Hirsch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89tienne_Hirsch "Étienne Hirsch") ([Hirsch Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hirsch_Commission "Hirsch Commission")).[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-40)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-41)

The OEEC was in turn reformed in 1961 into the [Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisation_for_Economic_Co-operation_and_Development "Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development") (OECD) and its membership was extended to states outside of Europe, the United States and Canada. During the 1960s, tensions began to show, with France seeking to limit supranational power. Nevertheless, in 1965 an agreement was reached, and on 1 July 1967 the [Merger Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merger_Treaty "Merger Treaty") created a single set of institutions for the three communities, which were collectively referred to as the _[European Communities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European\_Communities "European Communities")_.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-ENA_Merge-42)[Jean Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Rey_(politician) "Jean Rey (politician)")[presided over](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_European_Commission "President of the European Commission") the first merged commission ([Rey Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rey_Commission "Rey Commission")).[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-43)

### First enlargement and European co-operation (1973‍–‍1993)

Main article: [History of the European Communities (1973–1993)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_European_Communities_(1973%E2%80%931993) "History of the European Communities (1973–1993)")

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7d/Photograph_of_President_Gerald_R._Ford_and_Members_of_the_American_Delegation_Taking_a_Break_at_the_Conference_on_Security_and_Cooperation_in_Europe_in_Helsinki%2C_Finland_-_NARA_-_7462031.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Photograph_of_President_Gerald_R._Ford_and_Members_of_the_American_Delegation_Taking_a_Break_at_the_Conference_on_Security_and_Cooperation_in_Europe_in_Helsinki,_Finland_-_NARA_-_7462031.jpg)

[Gerald Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Ford "Gerald Ford") and the American delegation at the [CSCE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conference_on_Security_and_Co-operation_in_Europe "Conference on Security and Co-operation in Europe") (1975)

In 1973, the communities were enlarged to include [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark "Denmark") (including Greenland), Ireland, and the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accession_of_the_United_Kingdom_to_the_European_Communities "Accession of the United Kingdom to the European Communities").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-ENA_First_enlargement-44)[Norway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norway "Norway") had negotiated to join at the same time, but Norwegian voters rejected membership in a [referendum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Norwegian_European_Communities_membership_referendum "1972 Norwegian European Communities membership referendum"). The _[Ostpolitik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ostpolitik "Ostpolitik")_ and the ensuing détente led to establishment of a first truly pan-European body, the [Conference on Security and Co-operation in Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conference_on_Security_and_Co-operation_in_Europe "Conference on Security and Co-operation in Europe") (CSCE), predecessor of the modern [Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organization_for_Security_and_Co-operation_in_Europe "Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe") (OSCE). In 1979, the [first direct elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979_European_Parliament_election "1979 European Parliament election") to the European Parliament were held.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-ENA_New_Parliament-45)[Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece "Greece") joined in 1981. In 1985, Greenland [left the Communities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_Greenlandic_European_Communities_membership_referendum "1982 Greenlandic European Communities membership referendum"), following a dispute over fishing rights. During the same year, the [Schengen Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schengen_Agreement "Schengen Agreement") paved the way for the creation of open borders without passport controls between most member states and some non-member states.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-46) In 1986, the [Single European Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single_European_Act "Single European Act") was signed. Portugal and [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accession_Treaty_of_Spain_to_the_European_Economic_Community "Accession Treaty of Spain to the European Economic Community") joined in 1986.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-ENA_Enlargement_negotiations-47) In 1990, after [the fall of the Eastern Bloc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolutions_of_1989 "Revolutions of 1989"), the former [East Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Germany "East Germany") became part of the communities as part of a [reunified Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_reunification "German reunification").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-Europa_History_80-89-48)

### Treaties of Maastricht, Amsterdam and Nice (1993‍–‍2004)

Main article: [History of the European Union (1993–2004)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_European_Union_(1993%E2%80%932004) "History of the European Union (1993–2004)")

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/65/GER_%E2%80%94_BY_%E2%80%94_Regensburg_-_Donaumarkt_1_%28Museum_der_Bayerischen_Geschichte%3B_Vertrag_von_Maastricht%29_%28cropped%29.JPG/250px-GER_%E2%80%94_BY_%E2%80%94_Regensburg_-_Donaumarkt_1_%28Museum_der_Bayerischen_Geschichte%3B_Vertrag_von_Maastricht%29_%28cropped%29.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GER_%E2%80%94_BY_%E2%80%94_Regensburg_-_Donaumarkt_1_(Museum_der_Bayerischen_Geschichte;_Vertrag_von_Maastricht)_(cropped).JPG)

[Maastricht Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maastricht_Treaty "Maastricht Treaty") (1992), establishing the EU

The European Union was formally established when the [Maastricht Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maastricht_Treaty "Maastricht Treaty")—whose main architects were [Horst Köhler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horst_K%C3%B6hler "Horst Köhler"),[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-49)[Helmut Kohl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmut_Kohl "Helmut Kohl") and [François Mitterrand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Mitterrand "François Mitterrand")—came into force on 1 November 1993.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigDe_Burca201115-24)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-50) The treaty also gave the name _[European Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European\_Community "European Community")_ to the EEC, even if it was referred to as such before the treaty. With further enlargement planned to include the former [communist states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_state "Communist state") of Central and Eastern Europe, as well as [Cyprus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyprus "Cyprus") and [Malta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malta "Malta"), the [Copenhagen criteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copenhagen_criteria "Copenhagen criteria") for candidate members to join the EU were agreed upon in June 1993. The expansion of the EU introduced a new level of complexity and discord.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-51)

In 1995, Austria, Finland, and Sweden [joined](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_enlargement_of_the_European_Union "1995 enlargement of the European Union") the EU. In 2002, euro banknotes and coins replaced national currencies in 12 of the member states. Since then, the [eurozone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurozone "Eurozone") has increased to encompass 21 countries. The euro currency became the second-largest reserve currency in the world. In 2004, the EU saw [its biggest enlargement to date](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_enlargement_of_the_European_Union "2004 enlargement of the European Union") when Cyprus, the Czech Republic, [Estonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estonia "Estonia"), [Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary "Hungary"), [Latvia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvia "Latvia"), [Lithuania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuania "Lithuania"), [Malta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malta "Malta"), [Poland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poland "Poland"), Slovakia, and [Slovenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovenia "Slovenia") joined the union.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-Europa_History_00-52)

### Treaty of Lisbon and Brexit (2004‍–‍present)

Main article: [History of the European Union (2004–present)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_European_Union_(2004%E2%80%93present) "History of the European Union (2004–present)")

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/46/Tratado_de_Lisboa_13_12_2007_%2804%29.jpg/250px-Tratado_de_Lisboa_13_12_2007_%2804%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Tratado_de_Lisboa_13_12_2007_(04).jpg)

Signing ceremony of the [Treaty of Lisbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Lisbon "Treaty of Lisbon") (2007)

In 2007, Bulgaria and Romania became EU members. Later that year, Slovenia adopted the euro,[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-Europa_History_00-52) followed by Cyprus and Malta in 2008, Slovakia in 2009, Estonia in 2011, Latvia in 2014, Lithuania in 2015, Croatia in 2023 and Bulgaria in 2026. On 1 December 2009, the [Lisbon Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Lisbon "Treaty of Lisbon") entered into force and reformed many aspects of the EU. In particular, it changed the legal structure of the EU, merging the [EU three pillars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three_pillars_of_the_European_Union "Three pillars of the European Union") system into a single legal entity provisioned with a [legal personality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_personality "Legal personality"), created a permanent [president of the European Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_European_Council "President of the European Council"), the first of which was [Herman Van Rompuy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herman_Van_Rompuy "Herman Van Rompuy"), and strengthened the position of the [high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Representative_of_the_Union_for_Foreign_Affairs_and_Security_Policy "High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPiris2010448-53)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-54)

In 2012, the EU [received the Nobel Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Nobel_Peace_Prize "2012 Nobel Peace Prize") for having "contributed to the advancement of peace and reconciliation, democracy, and human rights in Europe".[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-55)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-56) In 2013, [Croatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia "Croatia") became the 28th EU member.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-57) From the beginning of the 2010s, the cohesion of the European Union has been tested by several issues, including the [euro area crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro_area_crisis "Euro area crisis"), [2015 European migrant crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_European_migrant_crisis "2015 European migrant crisis"), and [Brexit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brexit "Brexit").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-BBCUKREFRESLT-58) A [referendum in the UK on its membership of the European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_United_Kingdom_European_Union_membership_referendum "2016 United Kingdom European Union membership referendum") was held in 2016, with 51.9 per cent of participants voting to leave.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-NYTEUBrexit-59) The UK formally notified the European Council of its decision to leave on 29 March 2017, initiating the [formal withdrawal procedure for leaving the EU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Article_50_of_the_Treaty_on_European_Union "Article 50 of the Treaty on European Union"); following extensions to the process, the UK left the European Union on 31 January 2020, although most areas of EU law continued to apply to the UK for a transition period that lasted until 31 December 2020.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-60)

The early 2020s saw Denmark [abolishing one of its three opt-outs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Danish_European_Union_opt-out_referendum "2022 Danish European Union opt-out referendum") and Croatia [adopting the euro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_and_the_euro "Croatia and the euro"). After [the economic crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_recession "COVID-19 recession") caused by the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), the EU leaders agreed for the first time to create common debt to finance the European Recovery Program called [Next Generation EU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Next_Generation_EU "Next Generation EU") (NGEU).[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-61) On 24 February 2022, after massing on the borders of Ukraine, the [Russian Armed Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Armed_Forces "Russian Armed Forces") undertook an attempt for a full-scale invasion of Ukraine.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-62)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-63) The European Union imposed [heavy sanctions on Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_sanctions_during_the_Russo-Ukrainian_War#EU_sanctions "International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War") and agreed on a pooled military aid package to Ukraine for lethal weapons funded via the [European Peace Facility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Peace_Facility "European Peace Facility") off-budget instrument.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-64)

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0b/The_ancient_Roman_Agora_is_illuminated_during_the_Next_Gen_EU_event%2C_in_Athens%2C_Greece%2C_on_June_16%2C_2021.jpg/330px-The_ancient_Roman_Agora_is_illuminated_during_the_Next_Gen_EU_event%2C_in_Athens%2C_Greece%2C_on_June_16%2C_2021.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_ancient_Roman_Agora_is_illuminated_during_the_Next_Gen_EU_event,_in_Athens,_Greece,_on_June_16,_2021.jpg)

The ancient [Roman Agora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Agora "Roman Agora") in Athens illuminated with a Next Generation EU sign

NGEU is a European Commission [economic recovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_recovery "Economic recovery") package to support the EU member states to recover from the COVID-19 pandemic, in particular those that have been particularly hard hit. It is sometimes styled NextGenerationEU and Next Gen EU, and also called the European Union Recovery Instrument.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-65) Agreed in principle by the [European Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Council "European Council") on 21 July 2020 and adopted on 14 December 2020, the instrument is worth [€](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro "Euro")750 billion. NGEU will operate from 2021 to 2026,[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-66) and will be tied to the regular [2021–2027 budget of the EU's Multiannual Financial Framework](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiannual_Financial_Framework#2021%E2%80%932027_Financial_Framework_and_recovery_package "Multiannual Financial Framework") (MFF). The comprehensive NGEU and MFF packages are projected to reach €1824.3 billion.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-67)

Preparing the EU for a new great enlargement is one of its political priorities, with the goal of achieving 35 member states by 2030. Institutional and budgetary reforms are being discussed in order for the EU to be ready for the new members.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-68)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-69)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-70)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-71)

In December 2025, it was leaked that the [United States government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_government "United States government") would attempt to persuade "Austria, Hungary, Italy, and Poland" to depart the EU in a Brexit-type manner.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-DO_Trump_interfere_2025-12-09-72)

### Timeline

Since the [end of World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aftermath_of_World_War_II "Aftermath of World War II"), most [sovereign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sovereign_state "Sovereign state")[European countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_countries "European countries") have entered into treaties and thereby co-operated and harmonised policies (or _pooled sovereignty_) in an increasing number of areas, in the [European integration project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_integration "European integration") or the _construction of Europe_ ([French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"): _la construction européenne_). The following timeline outlines the legal inception of the European Union (EU)—the principal framework for this unification. The EU inherited many of its present [organisations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bodies_of_the_European_Union_and_Euratom "Bodies of the European Union and Euratom"), [institutions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institutions_of_the_European_Union "Institutions of the European Union"), and responsibilities from the [European Communities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Communities "European Communities") (EC), which were founded in the 1950s in the spirit of the [Schuman Declaration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schuman_Declaration "Schuman Declaration").

The **European Union** (**EU**) is a [political](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_union "Political union") and [economic union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_union "Economic union") of 27[member states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_state_of_the_European_Union "Member state of the European Union") that are [located primarily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography_of_the_European_Union "Geography of the European Union") in Europe.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-14)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-15) A [supranational union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supranational_union "Supranational union") with a total area of 4,233,255 km 2 (1,634,469 sq mi) and an estimated population of just under 452 million as of 2026,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-Population.EU-7)[its member states generated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_the_European_Union "Economy of the European Union") a nominal [gross domestic product](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_domestic_product "Gross domestic product") (GDP) of around €18.802 trillion in 2025, accounting for approximately one sixth of [global economic output](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_economic_output "Global economic output").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-16) The EU is often described as a _[sui generis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sui\_generis "Sui generis")_ political entity combining characteristics of both a [federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation "Federation") and a [confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confederation "Confederation").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-17)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-18)

Its cornerstone, the [Customs Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union_Customs_Union "European Union Customs Union"), paved the way to establishing [an internal single market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Single_Market "European Single Market") based on standardised [legal framework and legislation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union_law "European Union law") that apply in all member states in those matters, and only those matters, where the states have agreed to act as one. EU policies aim to ensure the free movement of people, goods, services and capital within the internal market;[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-Europa_Internal_Market-19) enact legislation in justice and home affairs; and maintain common policies on [trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_Commercial_Policy_(EU) "Common Commercial Policy (EU)"),[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-20)[agriculture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_Agricultural_Policy "Common Agricultural Policy"),[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-21)[fisheries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_Fisheries_Policy "Common Fisheries Policy"), and [regional development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regional_policy_of_the_European_Union "Regional policy of the European Union").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-22)

Passport controls have been abolished for travel within the [Schengen Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schengen_Area "Schengen Area").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-Internal_borders-23) The [eurozone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurozone "Eurozone") is a group composed of the 21 EU member states that have fully implemented the [EU's economic and monetary union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_and_Monetary_Union_of_the_European_Union "Economic and Monetary Union of the European Union") and use the [euro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro "Euro") currency. Through the [Common Foreign and Security Policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_Foreign_and_Security_Policy "Common Foreign and Security Policy"), the union has developed [a role in external relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_relations_of_the_European_Union "Foreign relations of the European Union") and [defence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_the_European_Union "Military of the European Union"). It maintains permanent [diplomatic missions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplomatic_missions_of_the_European_Union "Diplomatic missions of the European Union") throughout the world and represents itself at the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations"), the [World Trade Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Organization "World Trade Organization"), the [G7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union_and_the_G7 "European Union and the G7") and the [G20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G20 "G20"). In 2012, the EU [was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Nobel_Peace_Prize "2012 Nobel Peace Prize").

The EU was established, along with [its citizenship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union_citizenship "European Union citizenship"), when the [Maastricht Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maastricht_Treaty "Maastricht Treaty") came into force in 1993. The Union later acquired a single, explicit international legal personality with the entry into force of the [Treaty of Lisbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Lisbon "Treaty of Lisbon") in 2009.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigDe_Burca201115-24)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-25) Its beginnings can be traced to the [Inner Six](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inner_Six "Inner Six") states (Belgium, France, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, and [West Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Germany "West Germany")) at the start of modern [European integration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_integration "European integration") in 1948, and to the [Western Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Union_(alliance) "Western Union (alliance)"), the [International Authority for the Ruhr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Authority_for_the_Ruhr "International Authority for the Ruhr"), the [European Coal and Steel Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Coal_and_Steel_Community "European Coal and Steel Community"), the [European Economic Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Economic_Community "European Economic Community") and the [European Atomic Energy Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Atomic_Energy_Community "European Atomic Energy Community"), which were established by treaties. These increasingly amalgamated bodies grew, with their legal successor, the EU, both in size through [the accessions of a further 22 states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enlargement_of_the_European_Union "Enlargement of the European Union") from 1973 to 2013, and in power through acquisitions of policy areas. In 2020, [the United Kingdom became](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brexit "Brexit") the only member state to [leave the EU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Withdrawal_from_the_European_Union "Withdrawal from the European Union"); ten countries are [aspiring or negotiating to join it](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potential_enlargement_of_the_European_Union "Potential enlargement of the European Union").

### Background: World Wars and aftermath

Further information: [Ideas of European unity before 1948](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ideas_of_European_unity_before_1948 "Ideas of European unity before 1948")

[Internationalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internationalism_(politics) "Internationalism (politics)") and [visions of European unity had existed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ideas_of_European_unity_before_1948 "Ideas of European unity before 1948") since well before the 19th century, but gained particularly as a reaction to [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I") and its aftermath. In this light the first advances for the idea of [European integration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_integration "European integration") were made. In 1920 [John Maynard Keynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Maynard_Keynes "John Maynard Keynes") proposed a [European customs union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_customs_union "European customs union") for the struggling post-war European economies,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-Taussig_Keynes_1920_p._381-26) and in 1923 the oldest organisation for European integration, the [Paneuropean Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paneuropean_Union "Paneuropean Union") was founded, led by [Richard von Coudenhove-Kalergi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_von_Coudenhove-Kalergi "Richard von Coudenhove-Kalergi"), who would later found in June 1947 the [European Parliamentary Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Parliamentary_Union "European Parliamentary Union") (EPU). [Aristide Briand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aristide_Briand "Aristide Briand")—who was [Prime Minister of France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_France "Prime Minister of France"), a follower of the Paneuropean Union, and [Nobel Peace Prize laureate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_Peace_Prize_laureates "List of Nobel Peace Prize laureates") for the [Locarno Treaties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locarno_Treaties "Locarno Treaties")—delivered a widely recognised speech at the [League of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Nations "League of Nations") in [Geneva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geneva "Geneva") on 5 September 1929 for a [federal Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Europe "Federal Europe") to secure Europe and settle the historic [Franco-German enmity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco-German_enmity "Franco-German enmity").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-Schulz_2010_g046-27)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-Nelsson_2019_n549-28)

With large-scale war being waged in Europe once again in the 1930s and becoming [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), the question of what to fight against and what for had to be agreed on. A first agreement was the [Declaration of St James's Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_of_St_James's_Palace "Declaration of St James's Palace") of 1941, when [Europe's resistance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II_resistance "World War II resistance") gathered in London. This was expanded on by the 1941 [Atlantic Charter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Charter "Atlantic Charter"), establishing the [Allies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_II "Allies of World War II") and their common goals, inciting a new wave of global international institutions like the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") ([founded 1945](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Conference_on_International_Organization "United Nations Conference on International Organization")) or the [Bretton Woods System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bretton_Woods_System "Bretton Woods System") (1944).[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-Office_of_the_Historian_1946_r351-29)

In 1943 at the [Moscow Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow_Conference_(1943) "Moscow Conference (1943)") and [Tehran Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehran_Conference "Tehran Conference"), plans to establish joint institutions for a post-war world and Europe increasingly became a part of the agenda. This led to a decision at the [Yalta Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yalta_Conference "Yalta Conference") in 1944 to form a [European Advisory Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Advisory_Commission "European Advisory Commission"), later replaced by the [Council of Foreign Ministers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_Foreign_Ministers "Council of Foreign Ministers") and the [Allied Control Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allied_Control_Council "Allied Control Council"), following the German surrender and the [Potsdam Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potsdam_Agreement "Potsdam Agreement") in 1945.

By the end of the war, European integration became seen as an antidote to the [extreme nationalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extreme_nationalism "Extreme nationalism") that had caused the war.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-30) On 19 September 1946, in a much recognised speech, [Winston Churchill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill "Winston Churchill"), speaking at the [University of Zürich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Z%C3%BCrich "University of Zürich"), reiterated his calls since 1930 for a "European Union" and "Council of Europe", coincidentally[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-Union_of_European_Federalists_(UEF)-31) while the [Hertenstein Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hertensteiner_Cross "Hertensteiner Cross") of the [Union of European Federalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_of_European_Federalists "Union of European Federalists"),[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-32) one of the constituent members of the [European Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Movement_International "European Movement International"), was laying out its principles. One month later, the [French Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Union "French Union") was installed by the new [Fourth French Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourth_French_Republic "Fourth French Republic") to direct the [decolonisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decolonization "Decolonization") of [its colonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_colonies "French colonies") so that they would become parts of a European community.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-33)

By 1947, a growing rift between the western Allied Powers and the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") became evident as a result of the rigged [1947 Polish legislative election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1947_Polish_legislative_election "1947 Polish legislative election"), which constituted an open breach of the [Yalta Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yalta_Agreement "Yalta Agreement"). March of that year saw two important developments. First was the signing of the [Treaty of Dunkirk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Dunkirk "Treaty of Dunkirk") between [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France") and the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom"). The treaty assured mutual assistance in the event of future military aggression against either nation. Though it officially named Germany as a threat, in reality the actual concern was for the Soviet Union. A few days later came the announcement of the [Truman Doctrine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Truman_Doctrine "Truman Doctrine") which pledged American support for democracies to counter the Soviets.

### Initial years and the Paris Treaty (1948‍–‍1957)

Main article: [History of European integration (1948–1957)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_European_integration_(1948%E2%80%931957) "History of European integration (1948–1957)")

[Video 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/0/00/Schuman_Declaration.ogg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=rest&utm_content=original)

An excerpt of the [Schuman Declaration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schuman_Declaration "Schuman Declaration"), by [Robert Schuman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Schuman "Robert Schuman") on 9 May 1950 ([Europe Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe_Day "Europe Day"))

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5f/1951_CECA_ECSC.jpg/250px-1951_CECA_ECSC.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1951_CECA_ECSC.jpg)

[Treaty of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Paris_(1951) "Treaty of Paris (1951)") (1951), establishing the [ECSC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Coal_and_Steel_Community "European Coal and Steel Community")

Immediately following the [February 1948 coup d'état](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Czechoslovak_coup_d'%C3%A9tat "1948 Czechoslovak coup d'état") by the [Communist Party of Czechoslovakia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_Czechoslovakia "Communist Party of Czechoslovakia"), the [London Six-Power Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Six-Power_Conference "London Six-Power Conference") was held, resulting in the [Soviet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") boycott of the Allied Control Council and its incapacitation, an event marking the beginning of the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War"). The year 1948 marked the beginning of the institutionalised modern [European integration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_integration "European integration"). In March 1948 the [Treaty of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Brussels "Treaty of Brussels") was signed, establishing the [Western Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Union_(alliance) "Western Union (alliance)") (WU), followed by the [International Authority for the Ruhr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Authority_for_the_Ruhr "International Authority for the Ruhr"). Furthermore, the [Organisation for European Economic Co-operation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisation_for_European_Economic_Co-operation "Organisation for European Economic Co-operation") (OEEC), the predecessor of the OECD, was also founded in 1948 to manage the [Marshall Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_Plan "Marshall Plan"), which led to the Soviets creating [Comecon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comecon "Comecon") in response. The ensuing [Hague Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hague_Congress_(1948) "Hague Congress (1948)") of May 1948 was a pivotal moment in European integration, as it led to the creation of the [European Movement International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Movement_International "European Movement International"), the [College of Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_of_Europe "College of Europe"),[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-34) and most importantly to the foundation of the [Council of Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_Europe "Council of Europe") on 5 May 1949 (which is now [Europe Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe_Day "Europe Day")). The Council of Europe has since been a broad forum to further cooperation and shared issues, achieving, for example, the [European Convention on Human Rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Convention_on_Human_Rights "European Convention on Human Rights") in 1950.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-35)

Essential for the actual birth of the institutions of the EU was the [Schuman Declaration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schuman_Declaration "Schuman Declaration") on 9 May 1950 (the day after the fifth [Victory in Europe Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victory_in_Europe_Day "Victory in Europe Day")) and the decision by six nations (France, Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg, West Germany, and Italy) to follow Schuman and draft the [Treaty of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Paris_(1951) "Treaty of Paris (1951)"). This treaty was created in 1952 the [European Coal and Steel Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Coal_and_Steel_Community "European Coal and Steel Community") (ECSC), which was built on the [International Authority for the Ruhr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Authority_for_the_Ruhr "International Authority for the Ruhr"), installed by the Western Allies in 1949 to regulate the coal and steel industries of the Ruhr area in West Germany.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-36) Backed by the [Marshall Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_Plan "Marshall Plan") with large funds coming from the United States since 1948, the ECSC became a milestone organisation, enabling European economic development and integration and being the origin of the main institutions of the EU such as the [European Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Commission "European Commission") and [Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Parliament "European Parliament").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-37)

The [founding fathers of the European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Founding_fathers_of_the_European_Union "Founding fathers of the European Union") understood that coal and steel were the two industries essential for waging war, and believed that by tying their national industries together, a future war between their nations became much less likely.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-Europa_History_45-59-38) In parallel with Schuman, the [Pleven Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleven_Plan "Pleven Plan") of 1951 tried but failed to tie the institutions of the developing European community under the [European Political Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Political_Community_(1952) "European Political Community (1952)"), which was to include the also proposed [European Defence Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_establishing_the_European_Defence_Community "Treaty establishing the European Defence Community"), an alternative to [West Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Germany "West Germany") joining [NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO "NATO") which was established in 1949 under the [Truman Doctrine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Truman_Doctrine "Truman Doctrine"). In 1954 the [Modified Brussels Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modified_Brussels_Treaty "Modified Brussels Treaty") transformed the Western Union into the [Western European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_European_Union "Western European Union") (WEU). West Germany eventually joined both the WEU and NATO in 1955, prompting the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") to form the [Warsaw Pact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warsaw_Pact "Warsaw Pact") in 1955 as an institutional framework for its military domination in the countries of [Central and Eastern Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_and_Eastern_Europe "Central and Eastern Europe"). Assessing the progress of European integration the [Messina Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Messina_Conference "Messina Conference") was held in 1955, ordering the [Spaak Report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spaak_Report "Spaak Report"), which in 1956 recommended the next significant steps of European integration.

### Treaty of Rome (1958‍–‍1972)

Main article: [History of the European Communities (1958–1972)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_European_Communities_(1958%E2%80%931972) "History of the European Communities (1958–1972)")

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/59/Bundesarchiv_Bild_183-45653-0001%2C_Rom%2C_Vertr%C3%A4ge_%C3%BCber_Zollpakt_und_Eurotom_unterzeichnet.jpg/250px-Bundesarchiv_Bild_183-45653-0001%2C_Rom%2C_Vertr%C3%A4ge_%C3%BCber_Zollpakt_und_Eurotom_unterzeichnet.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bundesarchiv_Bild_183-45653-0001,_Rom,_Vertr%C3%A4ge_%C3%BCber_Zollpakt_und_Eurotom_unterzeichnet.jpg)

Signing ceremony of the [Treaty of Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Rome "Treaty of Rome") (1957), establishing the [EEC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Economic_Community "European Economic Community")

In 1957, [Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium "Belgium"), [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France"), [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy"), [Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxembourg "Luxembourg"), [the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands"), and [West Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Germany "West Germany") signed the [Treaty of Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Rome "Treaty of Rome"), which created the [European Economic Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Economic_Community "European Economic Community") (EEC) and established a [customs union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union_Customs_Union "European Union Customs Union").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-39) They also signed another pact creating the [European Atomic Energy Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Atomic_Energy_Community "European Atomic Energy Community") (Euratom) for cooperation in developing nuclear power. Both treaties came into force in 1958.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-Europa_History_45-59-38) Although the EEC and Euratom were created separately from the ECSC, they shared the same courts and the Common Assembly. The EEC was headed by [Walter Hallstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Hallstein "Walter Hallstein") ([Hallstein Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hallstein_Commission "Hallstein Commission")) and Euratom was headed by [Louis Armand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Armand "Louis Armand") ([Armand Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armand_Commission "Armand Commission")) and then [Étienne Hirsch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89tienne_Hirsch "Étienne Hirsch") ([Hirsch Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hirsch_Commission "Hirsch Commission")).[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-40)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-41)

The OEEC was in turn reformed in 1961 into the [Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisation_for_Economic_Co-operation_and_Development "Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development") (OECD) and its membership was extended to states outside of Europe, the United States and Canada. During the 1960s, tensions began to show, with France seeking to limit supranational power. Nevertheless, in 1965 an agreement was reached, and on 1 July 1967 the [Merger Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merger_Treaty "Merger Treaty") created a single set of institutions for the three communities, which were collectively referred to as the _[European Communities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European\_Communities "European Communities")_.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-ENA_Merge-42)[Jean Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Rey_(politician) "Jean Rey (politician)")[presided over](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_European_Commission "President of the European Commission") the first merged commission ([Rey Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rey_Commission "Rey Commission")).[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-43)

### First enlargement and European co-operation (1973‍–‍1993)

Main article: [History of the European Communities (1973–1993)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_European_Communities_(1973%E2%80%931993) "History of the European Communities (1973–1993)")

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7d/Photograph_of_President_Gerald_R._Ford_and_Members_of_the_American_Delegation_Taking_a_Break_at_the_Conference_on_Security_and_Cooperation_in_Europe_in_Helsinki%2C_Finland_-_NARA_-_7462031.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Photograph_of_President_Gerald_R._Ford_and_Members_of_the_American_Delegation_Taking_a_Break_at_the_Conference_on_Security_and_Cooperation_in_Europe_in_Helsinki,_Finland_-_NARA_-_7462031.jpg)

[Gerald Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Ford "Gerald Ford") and the American delegation at the [CSCE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conference_on_Security_and_Co-operation_in_Europe "Conference on Security and Co-operation in Europe") (1975)

In 1973, the communities were enlarged to include [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark "Denmark") (including Greenland), Ireland, and the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accession_of_the_United_Kingdom_to_the_European_Communities "Accession of the United Kingdom to the European Communities").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-ENA_First_enlargement-44)[Norway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norway "Norway") had negotiated to join at the same time, but Norwegian voters rejected membership in a [referendum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Norwegian_European_Communities_membership_referendum "1972 Norwegian European Communities membership referendum"). The _[Ostpolitik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ostpolitik "Ostpolitik")_ and the ensuing détente led to establishment of a first truly pan-European body, the [Conference on Security and Co-operation in Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conference_on_Security_and_Co-operation_in_Europe "Conference on Security and Co-operation in Europe") (CSCE), predecessor of the modern [Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organization_for_Security_and_Co-operation_in_Europe "Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe") (OSCE). In 1979, the [first direct elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979_European_Parliament_election "1979 European Parliament election") to the European Parliament were held.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-ENA_New_Parliament-45)[Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece "Greece") joined in 1981. In 1985, Greenland [left the Communities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_Greenlandic_European_Communities_membership_referendum "1982 Greenlandic European Communities membership referendum"), following a dispute over fishing rights. During the same year, the [Schengen Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schengen_Agreement "Schengen Agreement") paved the way for the creation of open borders without passport controls between most member states and some non-member states.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-46) In 1986, the [Single European Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single_European_Act "Single European Act") was signed. Portugal and [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accession_Treaty_of_Spain_to_the_European_Economic_Community "Accession Treaty of Spain to the European Economic Community") joined in 1986.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-ENA_Enlargement_negotiations-47) In 1990, after [the fall of the Eastern Bloc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolutions_of_1989 "Revolutions of 1989"), the former [East Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Germany "East Germany") became part of the communities as part of a [reunified Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_reunification "German reunification").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-Europa_History_80-89-48)

### Treaties of Maastricht, Amsterdam and Nice (1993‍–‍2004)

Main article: [History of the European Union (1993–2004)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_European_Union_(1993%E2%80%932004) "History of the European Union (1993–2004)")

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/65/GER_%E2%80%94_BY_%E2%80%94_Regensburg_-_Donaumarkt_1_%28Museum_der_Bayerischen_Geschichte%3B_Vertrag_von_Maastricht%29_%28cropped%29.JPG/250px-GER_%E2%80%94_BY_%E2%80%94_Regensburg_-_Donaumarkt_1_%28Museum_der_Bayerischen_Geschichte%3B_Vertrag_von_Maastricht%29_%28cropped%29.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GER_%E2%80%94_BY_%E2%80%94_Regensburg_-_Donaumarkt_1_(Museum_der_Bayerischen_Geschichte;_Vertrag_von_Maastricht)_(cropped).JPG)

[Maastricht Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maastricht_Treaty "Maastricht Treaty") (1992), establishing the EU

The European Union was formally established when the [Maastricht Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maastricht_Treaty "Maastricht Treaty")—whose main architects were [Horst Köhler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horst_K%C3%B6hler "Horst Köhler"),[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-49)[Helmut Kohl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmut_Kohl "Helmut Kohl") and [François Mitterrand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Mitterrand "François Mitterrand")—came into force on 1 November 1993.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigDe_Burca201115-24)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-50) The treaty also gave the name _[European Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European\_Community "European Community")_ to the EEC, even if it was referred to as such before the treaty. With further enlargement planned to include the former [communist states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_state "Communist state") of Central and Eastern Europe, as well as [Cyprus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyprus "Cyprus") and [Malta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malta "Malta"), the [Copenhagen criteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copenhagen_criteria "Copenhagen criteria") for candidate members to join the EU were agreed upon in June 1993. The expansion of the EU introduced a new level of complexity and discord.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-51)

In 1995, Austria, Finland, and Sweden [joined](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_enlargement_of_the_European_Union "1995 enlargement of the European Union") the EU. In 2002, euro banknotes and coins replaced national currencies in 12 of the member states. Since then, the [eurozone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurozone "Eurozone") has increased to encompass 21 countries. The euro currency became the second-largest reserve currency in the world. In 2004, the EU saw [its biggest enlargement to date](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_enlargement_of_the_European_Union "2004 enlargement of the European Union") when Cyprus, the Czech Republic, [Estonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estonia "Estonia"), [Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary "Hungary"), [Latvia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvia "Latvia"), [Lithuania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuania "Lithuania"), [Malta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malta "Malta"), [Poland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poland "Poland"), Slovakia, and [Slovenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovenia "Slovenia") joined the union.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union#cite_note-Europa_History_00-52)

### Treaty of Lisbon and Brexit (2004‍–‍present)

Main article: [History of the European Union (2004–present)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_European_Union_(2004%E2%80%93present) "History of the European Union (2004–present)")

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/46/Tratado_de_Lisboa_13_12_2007_%2804%29.jpg/250px-Tratado_de_Lisboa_13_12_2007_%2804%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Tratado_de_Lisboa_13_12_2007_(04).jpg)

In 2007, Bulgaria and Romania became EU members. **Hungary**[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-14) is a [landlocked country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landlocked_country "Landlocked country") in [Central Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Europe "Central Europe").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Flaw-15) Spanning much of the [Carpathian Basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannonian_Basin "Pannonian Basin"), it is bordered by Slovakia to the north, [Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine "Ukraine") to the northeast, [Romania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romania "Romania") to the east and southeast, [Serbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia "Serbia") to the south, [Croatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia "Croatia") and [Slovenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovenia "Slovenia") to the southwest, and [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria "Austria") to the west. Hungary lies within the [Danube River's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danube "Danube")[drainage basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drainage_basin "Drainage basin") and is dominated by great lowland [plains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plain "Plain"). It has a population of over 9.5 million, consisting mostly of ethnic [Hungarians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarians "Hungarians") (Magyars) and a [significant Romani minority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romani_people_in_Hungary "Romani people in Hungary"). [Hungarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_language "Hungarian language") is the [official language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Languages_of_Hungary "Languages of Hungary") and among the [few in Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Languages_of_Europe "Languages of Europe") outside the [Indo-European family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-European_languages "Indo-European languages").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-16)[Budapest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budapest "Budapest") is the country's capital, [largest city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_and_towns_of_Hungary "List of cities and towns of Hungary"), and cultural and economic center.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-17)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-18)

Before the establishment of the Hungarian state, the territory was settled by various groups, including [Celts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celts "Celts"), [Romans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Rome "Ancient Rome"), [Huns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huns "Huns"), [Germanic peoples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germanic_peoples "Germanic peoples"), [Avars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannonian_Avars "Pannonian Avars"), and [Slavs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavs "Slavs"). Statehood began in the late ninth century with the [Principality of Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principality_of_Hungary "Principality of Hungary"), which became a medieval [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian "Christian") kingdom under King [Stephen I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_I_of_Hungary "Stephen I of Hungary") in 1000. After it was defeated by the [Ottoman Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman_Empire "Ottoman Empire") at the [Battle of Mohács](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Moh%C3%A1cs "Battle of Mohács") in 1526, the kingdom was split into three regions for over 150 years until its reunion under [Habsburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habsburg "Habsburg") rule before the turn of the 18th century. Several uprisings against the Habsburgs precipitated the formation of the [Austro-Hungarian Monarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austro-Hungarian_Monarchy "Austro-Hungarian Monarchy") in the [Compromise of 1867](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austro-Hungarian_Compromise_of_1867 "Austro-Hungarian Compromise of 1867"); Austria-Hungary remained a European [great power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_power "Great power") until [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I"). Hungary's modern borders were then established by the 1920 [Treaty of Trianon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Trianon "Treaty of Trianon"), which resulted in severe losses for the country, including 71% of its historical territory and the majority of its economy and population; [a third of ethnic Hungarians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_diaspora "Hungarian diaspora") were left outside the new borders.

Hungary endured turmoil in the early [interwar period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary_between_the_World_Wars "Hungary between the World Wars"), culminating in the [national-conservative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_conservatism "National conservatism") regime of [regent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regent_of_Hungary "Regent of Hungary")[Miklós Horthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikl%C3%B3s_Horthy "Miklós Horthy"). Hungary joined the [Axis powers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axis_powers "Axis powers") in [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), suffering significant damage and casualties.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Montgomery-19)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Thomas,_pg._11-20) After a brief [Soviet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") occupation, the [Hungarian People's Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_People's_Republic "Hungarian People's Republic") was established in 1949 as a [satellite state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satellite_state "Satellite state") inside the [Warsaw Pact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warsaw_Pact "Warsaw Pact"). Subsequent political repression and economic stagnation led to the unsuccessful [Hungarian Revolution of 1956](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_Revolution_of_1956 "Hungarian Revolution of 1956"), though [communist rule softened](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goulash_Communism "Goulash Communism") in the following decades. During the [Revolutions of 1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolutions_of_1989 "Revolutions of 1989"), Hungary peacefully transitioned into a [democratic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_republic "Democratic republic")[parliamentary republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliamentary_republic "Parliamentary republic").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-21) It joined the European Union (EU) in 2004 and the [Schengen Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schengen_Area "Schengen Area") in 2007. [Under the leadership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_premiership_of_Viktor_Orb%C3%A1n "Second premiership of Viktor Orbán") of [Viktor Orbán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viktor_Orb%C3%A1n "Viktor Orbán") and [Fidesz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fidesz "Fidesz") from 2010 to 2026, the country experienced [democratic backsliding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_backsliding "Democratic backsliding").

Hungary is a [high-income economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank_high-income_economy "World Bank high-income economy") with [universal health care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Healthcare_in_Hungary "Healthcare in Hungary") and tuition-free [tertiary education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_universities_and_colleges_in_Hungary "List of universities and colleges in Hungary").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-auto-22)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-europa-23) It has a long history
